levels.title: Level 1: Taming Tight Coupling (SRP & OCP)
levels.description: A monolithic OrderProcessor violates SRP and blocks extension. Extract responsibilities and introduce polymorphism.
levels.initial_canvas:
classDiagram
class OrderProcessor {
    +processOrder(Order o)
    +calculateSalesTax(Order o)
    +saveToMySQL(Order o)
    +sendEmailConfirmation(Order o)
}
class MySQLDB
class SMTPClient
OrderProcessor --> MySQLDB : direct_write
OrderProcessor --> SMTPClient : direct_send

questions.text: The current OrderProcessor class violates SRP by managing three distinct business reasons to change (Data Persistence, Notification Delivery, and Tax Calculations). Which TWO separate components should we isolate to cleanly refactor this layout?
choices: An OrderRepository class tasked purely with structural database persistence mapping
An abstract NotificationService managing channel delivery variants
A global GlobalSingletonVariable holding active configuration metrics
A CacheManager processing memory lookup tables
correct_answer: An OrderRepository class tasked purely with structural database persistence mapping
An abstract NotificationService managing channel delivery variants
questions.explanation: Extracting persistence and notifications into their own dedicated classes separates core business logic from systemic infrastructure implementation concerns.

questions.text: The system needs to support expanding notification targets (Email, SMS, Slack pushing channels). To abide by the Open-Closed Principle (OCP), how should NotificationService be redesigned?
choices: Add inside-method if/else conditional strings checking notification types sequentially
Convert NotificationService into an interface, implementing concrete variants like EmailNotification and SMSNotification
Create separate independent worker services for every unique communication channel without sharing abstractions
questions.correct_answer: Convert NotificationService into an interface, implementing concrete variants like EmailNotification and SMSNotification
questions.explanation: By leveraging polymorphism through an interface, the architecture becomes open for extension (adding new alert types) but remains closed for modification (no need to change existing OrderProcessor execution arrays).

levels.title: Level 2: KISS & YAGNI Simplification
levels.description: A cart total feature was over-engineered with factories and observers for requirements that do not exist yet. Strip the noise.

questions.text: The requirement is only: return the sum of item prices in a cart. Which TWO layers are speculative abstractions that violate YAGNI and should be removed first?
choices: A single CartTotalService with one calculateTotal method
Unit tests for the cart sum
questions.explanation: Factories and observer networks solve problems you do not have yet. YAGNI says delete them until a real extension point is required.

questions.text: After removing speculative layers, what is the simplest design that still satisfies the requirement cleanly?
choices: Replace the hierarchy with one CartTotalService exposing calculateTotal(Cart c)
Move all logic into a static method on the Cart entity plus a database trigger
questions.correct_answer: Replace the hierarchy with one CartTotalService exposing calculateTotal(Cart c)
questions.explanation: KISS favors the smallest structure that is easy to read and test. One service with one method beats a facade wrapping a leftover class from a deleted factory.
